Mutations in SF3B4 impair spliceosome function, leading to craniofacial abnormalities. Concurrently, mutations in HNRNPA2B1 disrupt protein aggregation pathways, which in turn impairs autophagy. Dysfunctional autophagy can lead to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular dysfunction, manifesting as myopathy, frontotemporal dementia, and Paget disease of bone. The impaired spliceosome function from SF3B4 may also indirectly affect autophagy by disrupting the expression or function of key autophagy-related proteins.
